rows.description: A teenager yells during a quarrel with a parent or friend, driven by hurt, frustration or a wish to be heard. Taking a break, lowering the voice and returning to talk works better than escalating.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, hurt

rows.subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
rows.description: A teenager learns that a scream or yell for help should be taken seriously, even when it might be a prank. Checking safely and calling for help beats ignoring it; false alarms erode trust, so pranks should not use it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.subtype: Groaning, moaning and huffing at demands [Expressing]
rows.description: A teenager groans at homework or chores, meaning boredom, protest or stress. It rarely means real refusal; a light response and a clear expectation works better than a lecture, while a groan of real pain should be taken seriously.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: boredom, hurt
related concepts: boredom

rows.description: A teenager snorts or clears the throat, and peers may read it as mockery, warning or a real need. The sound is ambiguous; a child with a cold or a tic should not be blamed, and asking calmly avoids unfair conclusions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A teenager says huh as confusion, surprise or challenge and mm-hmm as listening, agreement or a brush-off. Tone and timing shape meaning, so a follow-up question is wiser than assuming the sound means yes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: confusion, surprise

rows.description: A teenager uses ugh for irritation, fatigue or dramatic humour. Others may take it as rudeness, but often it is harmless venting; a teen can learn to add a few words such as that was a long day to avoid confusion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, anger, confusion, tiredness
related concepts: humour

rows.subtype: Quiet voice under stress or shyness [Mismatch]
rows.description: A teenager speaks very softly at school, which teachers may read as low confidence, respect or disinterest. Reasons vary and include culture, shyness or fear, so encouragement and a quieter setting work better than criticism.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, fear, shyness, interest

rows.description: A teenager's voice deepens or cracks during puberty, causing embarrassment or jokes. Pitch changes are physical rather than emotional, and kind peers ignore the crack; adults reassure that it settles with time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: embarrassment

rows.description: A teenager may clip words or clear the throat to hide a choked voice when upset in front of peers. Trusted adults can offer a private moment instead of pressing for words in public.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: A teenager whose voice cracks during puberty may feel embarrassed though the crack is physical, not emotional. Listeners are wise to ignore it, and the teen can laugh it off rather than go silent.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, embarrassment
